name: Zhang Desheng
current_role: Founder and chairman, Zhejiang Wanma Group (controlling shareholder of Zhejiang Wanma Co., SZSE: 002276)
profile: Zhang Desheng founded the Wanma group in Lin'an, Hangzhou, which makes power cables and polymer materials via Zhejiang Wanma (listed 2009) and also controlled Wanma Technology (SZSE: 300698) at its 2017 IPO. Before going into business in 1989 he was deputy head of a farm-machinery factory. Wanma has expanded into EV charging.
interesting_fact: Forbes added him to its billionaire ranks in 2015 on investor hopes for Wanma's electric-vehicle charging business, an energy angle relevant to the podcast.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding his own business in 1989, Zhang was deputy head of a farm-machinery factory (per Forbes profile).
notes: Low public profile; no personal channels found. Some sources say his daughter Zhang Bin chairs the group's tech arm, so check current chair in latest SZSE filings. Best route is via the company's board secretary/IR office. Do not confuse him with the Shaanxi politician of the same name.

name: Ding Shui Po
current_role: Founder, chairman and CEO, Xtep International Holdings (HKEX: 1368)
profile: Ding Shui Po founded Xtep in Fujian in 1999. It began as a manufacturer for international brands before building its own Xtep sportswear brand, and it now also runs Saucony and Merrell in China. He has more than 30 years in the sportswear industry and remains chairman and CEO, with his daughter Ding Lizhi serving as group CFO.
interesting_fact: Xtep is a major Chinese running brand. Ding sits on the China Athletic Association's marathon committee (2015) and became a specially invited vice president of the association in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serial executive-education student: Peking U (2004), Tsinghua (2006), CKGSB (2011), CEIBS and Xiamen EMBA (2014), Harvard's Global CEO Program (2018), and CKGSB again in 2023. He was named EY Entrepreneur of the Year China in 2009.
notes: Best route is via Xtep investor relations / corporate communications (Hong Kong). Running/marathon angle could be a hook.
